claim: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients experience immune compromise characterized by complex alterations of both innate and adaptive immunity.
source: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients experience immune compromise characterized by complex alterations of both innate and adaptive immunity, and results in higher susceptibility to infection and lower response to vaccination.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characterization of ESRD patients, drawing on established scientific understanding.

claim: ESRD patients have higher susceptibility to infection.
source: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients experience immune compromise characterized by complex alterations of both innate and adaptive immunity, and results in higher susceptibility to infection and lower response to vaccination.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of immune compromise in ESRD patients, representing established knowledge.

claim: ESRD patients have lower response to vaccination.
source: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients experience immune compromise characterized by complex alterations of both innate and adaptive immunity, and results in higher susceptibility to infection and lower response to vaccination.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of immune compromise in ESRD patients, representing established knowledge.

claim: Transcriptomic analyses demonstrated differing time courses of immune responses in HD patients compared to controls.
source: Transcriptomic analyses demonstrated differing time courses of immune responses, with prolonged myeloid cell activity in HD at 1 wk after the first vaccination dose.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and BTM enrichment analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: HD patients showed prolonged myeloid cell activity at 1 week after the first vaccination dose.
source: Transcriptomic analyses demonstrated differing time courses of immune responses, with prolonged myeloid cell activity in HD at 1 wk after the first vaccination dose.
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis showing myeloid module enrichment at V1D7 in HD patients.

claim: HD patients demonstrated decreased metabolic activity compared to controls after the second vaccination dose.
source: HD also demonstrated decreased metabolic activity and decreased antigen presentation compared to controls after the second vaccination dose.
evidence: This is supported by direct comparison of gene expression between HD and controls at V2D7.

claim: HD patients demonstrated decreased antigen presentation compared to controls after the second vaccination dose.
source: HD also demonstrated decreased metabolic activity and decreased antigen presentation compared to controls after the second vaccination dose.
evidence: This is supported by direct comparison of gene expression between HD and controls at V2D7.

claim: Anti-spike IgG titers were substantially elevated in both controls and HD at V2D7.
source: Anti-spike IgG titers and neutralizing function were substantially elevated in both controls and HD at V2D7, with a small but significant reduction in titers in HD groups (p<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by anti-spike IgG ELISA measurements at V2D7.

claim: Neutralizing antibody function was substantially elevated in both controls and HD at V2D7.
source: Anti-spike IgG titers and neutralizing function were substantially elevated in both controls and HD at V2D7, with a small but significant reduction in titers in HD groups (p<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by antibody neutralization assays at V2D7.

claim: HD patients showed a small but significant reduction in anti-spike IgG titers compared to controls at V2D7 (p<0.05).
source: Anti-spike IgG titers and neutralizing function were substantially elevated in both controls and HD at V2D7, with a small but significant reduction in titers in HD groups (p<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparison of anti-spike IgG titers between groups at V2D7.

claim: Anti-spike IgG remained elevated above baseline at 6 months in both subject groups.
source: Anti-spike IgG remained elevated above baseline at 6 mo in both subject groups.
evidence: This is supported by anti-spike IgG measurements at 6 months (M6) compared to baseline (V1D0).

claim: Anti-spike IgG titers at V2D7 were highly predictive of 6-month titer levels.
source: Anti-spike IgG titers at V2D7 were highly predictive of 6-month titer levels.
evidence: This is supported by linear modeling showing V2D7 titers predict M6 titers.

claim: Transcriptomic biomarkers after the second vaccination dose were predictive of antibody development.
source: Transcriptomic biomarkers after the second vaccination dose and clinical biomarkers including ferritin levels were found to be predictive of antibody development.
evidence: This is supported by linear models showing BTM expression predicts anti-spike IgG levels.

claim: Clinical biomarkers including ferritin levels were predictive of antibody development.
source: Transcriptomic biomarkers after the second vaccination dose and clinical biomarkers including ferritin levels were found to be predictive of antibody development.
evidence: This is supported by linear models showing ferritin levels predict anti-spike IgG levels.

claim: The prevalence of ESRD in the United States reached 809,000 in 2019.
source: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) is the most advanced stage of chronic kidney disease (CKD), with prevalence in the United States reaching 809,000 in 2019 (Johansen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Johansen et al., 2022.

claim: Hemodialysis is the most used form of renal replacement therapy for ESRD patients in the United States.
source: The most used form of renal replacement therapy for ESRD patients in the United States is hemodialysis (HD).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ESRD treatment in the US.

claim: The mortality rate in ESRD patients is as high as 20% annually.
source: Despite significant improvements in HD technology, the mortality rate in ESRD patients is still as high as 20% annually (Williams et al., 2004), with infections being the most common cause of hospitalization and mortality after cardiovascular disease (Kato et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Williams et al., 2004.

claim: Infections are the most common cause of hospitalization in ESRD patients after cardiovascular disease.
source: Despite significant improvements in HD technology, the mortality rate in ESRD patients is still as high as 20% annually (Williams et al., 2004), with infections being the most common cause of hospitalization and mortality after cardiovascular disease (Kato et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kato et al., 2008.

claim: Infections are the most common cause of mortality in ESRD patients after cardiovascular disease.
source: Despite significant improvements in HD technology, the mortality rate in ESRD patients is still as high as 20% annually (Williams et al., 2004), with infections being the most common cause of hospitalization and mortality after cardiovascular disease (Kato et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kato et al., 2008.

claim: The immunocompromised state of ESRD is characterized by simultaneous immunodepression and immunoactivation.
source: The immunocompromised state of ESRD is characterized by simultaneous immunodepression due to the impact of uremic milieu on immunocompetent cells and immunoactivation due to the accumulation of proinflammatory cytokines (Kato et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kato et al., 2008.

claim: ESRD is characterized by elevated levels of mannose-binding lectin.
source: There are alterations to both innate and adaptive immunity, including elevated levels of mannose-binding lectin (Satomura et al., 2002), impaired maturation of monocytes and dendritic cells (Satomura et al., 2002; Lim et al., 2007), increased B cell apoptosis (Fernández-Fresnedo et al., 2000), and decreased T-cell proliferation with elevated Th1/Th2 ratio (Stenvinkel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Satomura et al., 2002.

claim: ESRD is characterized by impaired maturation of monocytes and dendritic cells.
source: There are alterations to both innate and adaptive immunity, including elevated levels of mannose-binding lectin (Satomura et al., 2002), impaired maturation of monocytes and dendritic cells (Satomura et al., 2002; Lim et al., 2007), increased B cell apoptosis (Fernández-Fresnedo et al., 2000), and decreased T-cell proliferation with elevated Th1/Th2 ratio (Stenvinkel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Satomura et al., 2002 and Lim et al., 2007.

claim: ESRD is characterized by increased B cell apoptosis.
source: There are alterations to both innate and adaptive immunity, including elevated levels of mannose-binding lectin (Satomura et al., 2002), impaired maturation of monocytes and dendritic cells (Satomura et al., 2002; Lim et al., 2007), increased B cell apoptosis (Fernández-Fresnedo et al., 2000), and decreased T-cell proliferation with elevated Th1/Th2 ratio (Stenvinkel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fernández-Fresnedo et al., 2000.

claim: ESRD is characterized by decreased T-cell proliferation with elevated Th1/Th2 ratio.
source: There are alterations to both innate and adaptive immunity, including elevated levels of mannose-binding lectin (Satomura et al., 2002), impaired maturation of monocytes and dendritic cells (Satomura et al., 2002; Lim et al., 2007), increased B cell apoptosis (Fernández-Fresnedo et al., 2000), and decreased T-cell proliferation with elevated Th1/Th2 ratio (Stenvinkel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stenvinkel et al., 2005.

claim: ESRD patients show upregulation of genes involved in complement and oxidative metabolism pathways.
source: One study found upregulation of genes involved in the complement and oxidative metabolism pathways, and downregulation of genes associated with the clathrin-coated vesicle endosomal pathway and T-cell receptor signaling (Scherer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scherer et al., 2013.

claim: ESRD patients show downregulation of genes associated with the clathrin-coated vesicle endosomal pathway.
source: One study found upregulation of genes involved in the complement and oxidative metabolism pathways, and downregulation of genes associated with the clathrin-coated vesicle endosomal pathway and T-cell receptor signaling (Scherer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scherer et al., 2013.

claim: ESRD patients show downregulation of genes associated with T-cell receptor signaling.
source: One study found upregulation of genes involved in the complement and oxidative metabolism pathways, and downregulation of genes associated with the clathrin-coated vesicle endosomal pathway and T-cell receptor signaling (Scherer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scherer et al., 2013.

claim: ESRD patients demonstrate impaired expression of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial function.
source: Two other studies have demonstrated impaired expression of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial function (Granata et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Granata et al., 2009 and Liu et al., 2002.

claim: Maintenance HD patients show unique gene expression alterations compared to un-dialyzed CKD patients.
source: A study identifying a group of inflammatory genes playing a causative role in oxidative stress in dialysis patients showed unique gene expression alterations in maintenance HD patients compared to un-dialyzed CKD patients and compared to patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (Zaza et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zaza et al., 2008.

claim: Maintenance HD patients show unique gene expression alterations compared to patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
source: A study identifying a group of inflammatory genes playing a causative role in oxidative stress in dialysis patients showed unique gene expression alterations in maintenance HD patients compared to un-dialyzed CKD patients and compared to patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (Zaza et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zaza et al., 2008.

claim: Immune alterations in ESRD may lead to higher susceptibility to infection and lower response to vaccination.
source: These studies indicate a range of immune pathways that may impair vaccination response, and further suggest that dialysis leads to unique immune profile alterations. These alterations may lead to higher susceptibility to infection and lower response to vaccination (Ghadiani et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ghadiani et al., 2012 and represents an inference from prior studies.

claim: More than 90% of patients without CKD develop protective antibodies against HBV after vaccination.
source: For example, while more than 90% of patients without CKD develop protective antibodies against HBV after vaccination, only 50–60% of patients with ESRD seroconvert.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about HBV vaccination response.

claim: Only 50-60% of patients with ESRD seroconvert after HBV vaccination.
source: For example, while more than 90% of patients without CKD develop protective antibodies against HBV after vaccination, only 50–60% of patients with ESRD seroconvert.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about HBV vaccination response in ESRD.

claim: ESRD patients have higher vaccination failure rates against influenza virus.
source: There have also been higher vaccination failure rates demonstrated against influenza virus, Clostridium tetani, and Corynebacterium diphtheriae in ESRD (Eleftheriadis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Eleftheriadis et al., 2007.

claim: ESRD patients have higher vaccination failure rates against Clostridium tetani.
source: There have also been higher vaccination failure rates demonstrated against influenza virus, Clostridium tetani, and Corynebacterium diphtheriae in ESRD (Eleftheriadis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Eleftheriadis et al., 2007.

claim: ESRD patients have higher vaccination failure rates against Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
source: There have also been higher vaccination failure rates demonstrated against influenza virus, Clostridium tetani, and Corynebacterium diphtheriae in ESRD (Eleftheriadis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Eleftheriadis et al., 2007.

claim: BNT162b2 vaccine showed 95% reduction of COVID-19 disease in recipients.
source: The COVID-19 mRNA-based vaccines, BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273, have proven to be efficacious in non-immunocompromised individuals, with initial reports showing 95 and 94.1% reduction of COVID-19 disease in recipients (Baden et al., 2021; Polack et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baden et al., 2021 and Polack et al., 2020.

claim: mRNA-1273 vaccine showed 94.1% reduction of COVID-19 disease in recipients.
source: The COVID-19 mRNA-based vaccines, BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273, have proven to be efficacious in non-immunocompromised individuals, with initial reports showing 95 and 94.1% reduction of COVID-19 disease in recipients (Baden et al., 2021; Polack et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baden et al., 2021 and Polack et al., 2020.

claim: Recent studies of the SARS-CoV-2 BTN162b2 vaccine in HD demonstrate high levels of seroconversion ranging from 84 to 96%.
source: While recent studies of the SARS-CoV-2 BTN162b2 vaccine in HD demonstrate high levels of seroconversion ranging from 84 to 96% (Grupper et al., 2021; Jahn et al., 2021; Attias et al., 2021; Anand et al., 2021), they also demonstrate quantitatively reduced SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grupper et al., 2021; Jahn et al., 2021; Attias et al., 2021; Anand et al., 2021.

claim: Recent studies demonstrate quantitatively reduced SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies in HD patients after BTN162b2 vaccination.
source: While recent studies of the SARS-CoV-2 BTN162b2 vaccine in HD demonstrate high levels of seroconversion ranging from 84 to 96% (Grupper et al., 2021; Jahn et al., 2021; Attias et al., 2021; Anand et al., 2021), they also demonstrate quantitatively reduced SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grupper et al., 2021; Jahn et al., 2021; Attias et al., 2021; Anand et al., 2021.

claim: The study was approved by the University of Illinois at Chicago IRB (#2018-1038) Ethics Review Committee.
source: The study was approved by the University of Illinois at Chicago IRB (#2018-1038) Ethics Review Committee.
evidence: This is a direct statement about study approval.

claim: Maintenance HD patients were recruited from the outpatient HD unit at the University of Illinois Hospital in Chicago, IL.
source: Maintenance HD patients undergoing vaccination with the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in February 2021 were recruited from the outpatient HD unit at the University of Illinois Hospital (UIH) in Chicago, IL.
evidence: This describes the recruitment location for HD patients.

claim: Control subjects consisted of UIH employees undergoing BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccination.
source: Control subjects consisted of UIH employees undergoing BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccination at UIH from December 2020 to January 2021 with no self-reported history of kidney disease or immune disorders.
evidence: This describes the control subject recruitment.

claim: Control subjects had no self-reported history of kidney disease or immune disorders.
source: Control subjects consisted of UIH employees undergoing BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccination at UIH from December 2020 to January 2021 with no self-reported history of kidney disease or immune disorders.
evidence: This describes the inclusion criteria for control subjects.

claim: The second vaccination dose was administered 3 weeks apart from the first dose.
source: Blood was collected at 0–48 hr prior to and at multiple time points after both the first (V1) and second vaccination doses (V2), which were administered 3 wk apart.
evidence: This describes the vaccination schedule.

claim: Control samples were collected prior to each vaccination dose (D0) and at 1 d (D1) and 7 d (D7) after each dose.
source: Control samples were collected prior to each vaccination dose (D0) and at 1 d (D1) and 7 d (D7) after each dose, corresponding to six time points: V1D0, V1D1, V1D7, V2D0, V2D1, and V2D7.
evidence: This describes the sample collection schedule for controls.

claim: Blood was collected from HD subjects prior to each vaccination dose and at 2 d (D2) and 7 d after each dose.
source: Blood was collected from HD subjects prior to each vaccination dose and at 2 d (D2) and 7 d after each dose, corresponding to six time points: V1D0, V1D2, V1D7, V2D0, V2D2, and V2D7.
evidence: This describes the sample collection schedule for HD subjects.

claim: A final blood sample was drawn 6 months after initial vaccination for measurement of antibody titers.
source: A final blood sample was drawn 6 mo after initial vaccination (M6) for measurement of antibody titers, prior to additional vaccination doses.
evidence: This describes the 6-month follow-up sample collection.

claim: Serum and PBMCs were extracted within 2 hours of blood collection.
source: Serum and PBMCs were extracted within 2 hr of blood collection, then stored at –80°C.
evidence: This describes the sample processing protocol.

claim: PBMCs were extracted using density gradient centrifugation at 400 × g with Ficoll–Paque PLUS.
source: PBMCs were extracted using density gradient centrifugation at 400 × g with Ficoll–Paque PLUS.
evidence: This describes the PBMC extraction method.

claim: Ferritin levels 200-1200 ng/ml have been shown to be associated with lowest all-cause mortality in HD patients.
source: Within our analyses, ferritin was coded as either low risk (200–1200 ng/ml) or high risk (<200 or >1200 ng/ml) since ferritin levels 200–1200 ng/ml have been shown to be associated with lowest all-cause mortality in HD patients (Kalantar-Zadeh et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kalantar-Zadeh et al., 2005.

claim: RNA sequencing was performed on PBMCs at all V1 and V2 time points for all subjects for whom RNA libraries were successfully built at >5 time points.
source: RNA sequencing was performed on PBMCs at all V1 and V2 time points for all subjects for whom RNA libraries were successfully built at >5 time points.
evidence: This describes the RNA sequencing sample selection criteria.

claim: RNA samples with RIN ≥ 8 were used for sequencing.
source: Each RNA sample was quantified using the Qubit RNA High Sensitivity kit (Invitrogen) and Bioanalyzer RNA Pico kit (Agilent) with RIN ≥ 8.
evidence: This describes the RNA quality threshold for sequencing.

claim: There are substantially more differentially expressed genes in response to V2 compared to V1.
source: There are substantially more differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in response to V2 compared to V1, and at D1 and D2 post-vaccination compared to D7 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There are substantially more differentially expressed genes at D1 and D2 post-vaccination compared to D7.
source: There are substantially more differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in response to V2 compared to V1, and at D1 and D2 post-vaccination compared to D7 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: For HC, the largest number of DEGs is found at V2D1 (3974).
source: For HC, the largest number of DEGs is found at V2D1 (3974), indicating the most transcriptional activity immediately after the second vaccine dose, followed by V2D7 (177), V1D1 (128), and V1D7 (10).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis.

claim: For HD, the largest number of DEGs is found at V2D2 (1,111).
source: HD follows a similar pattern, with the largest number of DEGs found at V2D2 (1,111), followed by V2D7 (153), V1D2 (68), and V1D7 (8).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis.

claim: HD subjects with no SARS-CoV-2 history have substantially lower numbers of DEGs than HD subjects with positive SARS-CoV-2 history at each time point.
source: Notably, HD subjects with no SARS-CoV-2 history (n = 6) have substantially lower numbers of DEGs than HD subjects with positive SARS-CoV-2 history (n = 6) at each time point, and particularly at V2 time points (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Direct comparison of gene expression between HC and HD with no prior SARS-CoV-2 infection at V1D7 yielded five DEGs.
source: Direct comparison of gene expression between HC and HD with no prior reported SARS-CoV-2 infection at V1D7 yielded five DEGs in HD versus HC including increased expression of chemokine CCL19 in HD (p<0.05, FDR-corrected).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis comparing groups.

claim: HD showed increased expression of chemokine CCL19 compared to HC at V1D7.
source: Direct comparison of gene expression between HC and HD with no prior reported SARS-CoV-2 infection at V1D7 yielded five DEGs in HD versus HC including increased expression of chemokine CCL19 in HD (p<0.05, FDR-corrected).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Comparison of HC and HD at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs.
source: Comparison of these same groups at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs including increased expression in HD of TIA1, which encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes (Anderson et al., 1990) and natural killer cells, and BH3, a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis (Labi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis comparing groups.

claim: HD showed increased expression of TIA1 compared to HC at V2D7.
source: Comparison of these same groups at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs including increased expression in HD of TIA1, which encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes (Anderson et al., 1990) and natural killer cells, and BH3, a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis (Labi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis and citations to Anderson et al., 1990 and Labi et al., 2008.

claim: TIA1 encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes and natural killer cells.
source: Comparison of these same groups at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs including increased expression in HD of TIA1, which encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes (Anderson et al., 1990) and natural killer cells, and BH3, a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis (Labi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Anderson et al., 1990.

claim: HD showed increased expression of BH3 compared to HC at V2D7.
source: Comparison of these same groups at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs including increased expression in HD of TIA1, which encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes (Anderson et al., 1990) and natural killer cells, and BH3, a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis (Labi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis and a citation to Labi et al., 2008.

claim: BH3 is a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis.
source: Comparison of these same groups at V2D7 yielded 18 DEGs including increased expression in HD of TIA1, which encodes a granule-associated protein expressed in cytolytic lymphocytes (Anderson et al., 1990) and natural killer cells, and BH3, a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member and mediator of lymphocyte apoptosis (Labi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Labi et al., 2008.

claim: HC demonstrate early (V1D1) enrichment of 29 BTMs following V1.
source: Following V1, HC demonstrate early (V1D1) enrichment of 29 BTMs, with substantial upregulation of monocyte and antiviral IFN activity (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC show substantial upregulation of monocyte and antiviral IFN activity at V1D1.
source: Following V1, HC demonstrate early (V1D1) enrichment of 29 BTMs, with substantial upregulation of monocyte and antiviral IFN activity (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC demonstrate V1D7 enrichment of four BTMs including significant T cell activation.
source: The immune response transitions to V1D7 enrichment of four BTMs including significant T cell activation and downregulation of monocytes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC show downregulation of monocytes at V1D7.
source: The immune response transitions to V1D7 enrichment of four BTMs including significant T cell activation and downregulation of monocytes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC demonstrate early (V2D1) enrichment of 82 BTMs following V2.
source: Following V2, HC demonstrate early (V2D1) enrichment of 82 BTMs, with substantial upregulation of innate antiviral activity, similarly to V1D1 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC show substantial upregulation of innate antiviral activity at V2D1, similar to V1D1.
source: Following V2, HC demonstrate early (V2D1) enrichment of 82 BTMs, with substantial upregulation of innate antiviral activity, similarly to V1D1 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HC demonstrate V2D7 enrichment of ten BTMs with significant upregulation of plasma cells and immunoglobulins.
source: The immune response transitions to V2D7 enrichment of ten BTMs, with significant upregulation of plasma cells and immunoglobulins (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HD demonstrate early (V1D2) enrichment of 12 BTMs after the first vaccination dose.
source: In contrast, HD demonstrate early (V1D2) enrichment of 12 BTMs after the first vaccination dose, most significantly involving upregulation of innate antiviral responses (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: HD show upregulation of innate antiviral responses at V1D2.
source: In contrast, HD demonstrate early (V1D2) enrichment of 12 BTMs after the first vaccination dose, most significantly involving upregulation of innate antiviral responses (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HD demonstrate V1D7 enrichment of 17 BTMs with substantial upregulation of myeloid modules.
source: The immune response transitions to V1D7 enrichment of 17 BTMs, with substantial upregulation of myeloid modules (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The V1D7-positive enrichment of monocyte/myeloid modules in HD contrasts the negative enrichment of these modules in HC.
source: The V1D7-positive enrichment of monocyte/myeloid modules in HD contrast the negative enrichment of these modules in HC (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis comparing groups shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: HD demonstrate early (V2D2) enrichment of 27 BTMs following the second vaccination dose.
source: Following the second vaccination dose, HD demonstrate early (V2D2) enrichment of 27 BTMs most significantly involving upregulation of dendritic cell activity and proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HD show upregulation of dendritic cell activity and proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines at V2D2.
source: Following the second vaccination dose, HD demonstrate early (V2D2) enrichment of 27 BTMs most significantly involving upregulation of dendritic cell activity and proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: HD demonstrate V2D7 enrichment of one BTM: PLK signaling events.
source: The immune response progresses to V2D7 enrichment of one BTM: PLK signaling events (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: HD with positive SARS-CoV-2 demonstrated notable upregulation of plasma cell activity at V1D7.
source: While there were no significant BTM enrichments in HC with positive SARS-CoV-2 history, most likely due to the insufficient number of subjects, BTM enrichments for HD with positive SARS-CoV-2 demonstrated notable upregulation of plasma cell activity at V1D7.
evidence: This is supported by BTM enrichment analysis.

claim: All subjects demonstrated an increase in anti-spike IgG at V2D7.
source: All subjects demonstrated an increase in anti-spike IgG at V2D7, with titers for all subjects except one still elevated above baseline at six months.
evidence: This is supported by anti-spike IgG ELISA measurements.

claim: Titers for all subjects except one were still elevated above baseline at six months.
source: All subjects demonstrated an increase in anti-spike IgG at V2D7, with titers for all subjects except one still elevated above baseline at six months.
evidence: This is supported by anti-spike IgG measurements at M6.

claim: One HD subject with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection demonstrated the highest baseline titers of all subjects prior to vaccination.
source: The exception was one HD subject with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection who demonstrated the highest baseline titers of all subjects prior to vaccination.
evidence: This is supported by anti-spike IgG measurements at V1D0.

claim: Both HC and HD subjects demonstrated a statistically significant increase in anti-spike IgG from V1D0 to V2D7 (p<0.001).
source: Both HC and HD subjects demonstrated a statistically significant increase in anti-spike IgG and neutralization activity (ID50) from V1D0 to V2D7 (p<0.001), followed by an expected decrease at M6 from V2D7 levels (p<0.001) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of anti-spike IgG measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: Both HC and HD subjects demonstrated a statistically significant increase in neutralization activity (ID50) from V1D0 to V2D7 (p<0.001).
source: Both HC and HD subjects demonstrated a statistically significant increase in anti-spike IgG and neutralization activity (ID50) from V1D0 to V2D7 (p<0.001), followed by an expected decrease at M6 from V2D7 levels (p<0.001) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of neutralization assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: Anti-spike IgG showed an expected decrease at M6 from V2D7 levels (p<0.001).
source: Both HC and HD subjects demonstrated a statistically significant increase in anti-spike IgG and neutralization activity (ID50) from V1D0 to V2D7 (p<0.001), followed by an expected decrease at M6 from V2D7 levels (p<0.001) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of anti-spike IgG measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: M6 titers were still increased compared to baseline (p<0.001).
source: Despite this decrease, M6 titers were still increased compared to baseline (p<0.001).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of anti-spike IgG measurements.

claim: Higher anti-spike IgG at V2D7 was significantly predicted by higher pre-vaccination anti-spike IgG (p<0.01).
source: Higher anti-spike IgG at V2D7 was significantly predicted by higher pre-vaccination anti-spike IgG, control group assignment, and younger age (p<0.01, p<0.05, p<0.05, respectively), while gender, race, and ethnicity were not.
evidence: This is supported by linear modeling of anti-spike IgG predictors.

claim: Higher anti-spike IgG at V2D7 was significantly predicted by control group assignment (p<0.05).
source: Higher anti-spike IgG at V2D7 was significantly predicted by higher pre-vaccination anti-spike IgG, control group assignment, and younger age (p<0.01, p<0.05, p<0.05, respectively), while gender, race, and ethnicity were not.
evidence: This is supported by linear modeling of anti-spike IgG predictors.
